findings.title: Missing Content-Security-Policy (CSP) Header
findings.plainLanguageExplanation: Your website lacks a security policy that specifies which scripts are allowed to run. If an attacker injects malicious JavaScript, the browser will execute it without warning.
findings.technicalDetails: No Content-Security-Policy header detected in response headers. Susceptible to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) and malicious script injection.
findings.recommendation: Define a strict Content-Security-Policy header restricting script-src, object-src, and frame-ancestors.

findings.title: Missing Clickjacking Protection (X-Frame-Options)
findings.plainLanguageExplanation: Other websites can embed your login or checkout page inside an invisible frame, tricking users into clicking buttons they did not intend to click.
findings.technicalDetails: Missing X-Frame-Options: DENY or SAMEORIGIN directive.

findings.title: Server Technology Banner Disclosure
findings.plainLanguageExplanation: Your server is broadcasting the exact software version it runs (Vercel). This helps attackers search for known exploits for that exact version.
findings.technicalDetails: Server or X-Powered-By header reveals backend technology fingerprint.
findings.recommendation: Disable Server tokens in Nginx/Apache configuration and call app.disable("x-powered-by") in Express.

findings.title: Missing X-Content-Type-Options Header
findings.plainLanguageExplanation: Browsers may try to guess the file type instead of obeying the header, which can allow an uploaded text or image file to execute as JavaScript.

testsPerformed: Streaming Master S3 Access Policy Audit

findings.title: Missing Digital Rights Management (DRM) on 4K Stream Chunks
findings.plainLanguageExplanation: Your 4K video streams are delivered without hardware DRM encryption. Anyone with a browser extension can download full uncompressed movies without authorization.
findings.technicalDetails: High-resolution playlists are served as unencrypted MPEG-TS/fMP4 chunks. Widevine Modular and FairPlay Streaming keys are not enforced on premium tiers.
findings.recommendation: Implement Google Widevine and Apple FairPlay DRM licensing keys via Cloudflare Stream or AWS Elemental MediaConvert.

findings.title: Streaming URL Token Expiry Exceeds 24 Hours
findings.plainLanguageExplanation: When a paid user starts a movie, their playback link stays valid for 24 hours. They can share this link with friends or on social media.
findings.technicalDetails: HMAC signed token TTL in stream manifests is set to 86,400 seconds. Recommended duration is 3,600 to 7,200 seconds with IP binding.
findings.recommendation: Reduce token expiration to 60-120 minutes and regenerate tokens dynamically during player heartbeat requests.

findings.title: Content Storage Bucket Allows Anonymous Read on Preview Trailers
findings.plainLanguageExplanation: The cloud storage bucket holding promotional trailers is completely public. While intended for marketing, public read permissions should be restricted to CDN edge IPs.
findings.technicalDetails: Bucket policy allows s3:GetObject to Principal: *. Recommended pattern is AWS CloudFront Origin Access Control (OAC).
findings.recommendation: Configure CloudFront Origin Access Control (OAC) and remove public S3 bucket policies.

summary.executiveSummary: CineChain streaming architecture demonstrates solid web fundamentals but requires DRM encryption hardening for 4K assets and shorter CDN token lifespans.
keyRisks: High Risk of 4K Video Stream Piracy and Stream Ripping
Prolonged 24-hour token replay window on CDN playback manifests
topRecommendations: Enable Widevine/FairPlay DRM encryption on 4K video packaging
Reduce CDN playback URL token validity to 2 hours maximum
Apply CloudFront Origin Access Control (OAC) on media storage

limitations: Automated testing does not simulate hardware-level HDMI HDCP strippers
Testing performed on staging environment endpoints

findings.title: Missing Copyright Registration Date in E-book Spine Metadata
findings.plainLanguageExplanation: The inside packaging of the digital EPUB file lists the author but omits the explicit publication date metadata tag.
findings.technicalDetails: dc:date tag is missing in META-INF/container.opf. While harmless, major e-readers and public libraries use this tag to catalog release years.
findings.recommendation: Add <dc:date>2026-11-01</dc:date> to the OPF metadata template.

summary.executiveSummary: Veritas Publishing exhibits excellent digital provenance standards. All manuscripts are correctly hashed off-chain with SHA-256 fingerprints anchored on Base blockchain.
keyRisks: Minor metadata tagging omissions in legacy e-book files
topRecommendations: Incorporate Dublin Core metadata automated validator in publishing pipeline

limitations: Verification relies on authenticated publisher identity submissions

findings.title: Reentrancy Vulnerability in emergencyWithdraw()
findings.plainLanguageExplanation: The contract sends tokens to a user before subtracting their deposited balance. A malicious contract can re-enter this function repeatedly and drain the entire vault balance.
findings.technicalDetails: Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern is violated at line 142. External call `IERC20(asset).transfer(msg.sender, amount)` executes before `userBalances[msg.sender] = 0`.
findings.recommendation: Zero out the user balance BEFORE making the external transfer, or add OpenZeppelin nonReentrant modifier.

findings.title: Authentication Using Vulnerable tx.origin
findings.plainLanguageExplanation: The function checks `tx.origin == admin`. If the admin accidentally approves a malicious transaction on a compromised website, the attacker can hijack the admin role.
findings.technicalDetails: Use of tx.origin allows intermediate contract calls to pass authorization checks. Phishing attack vector SWC-115.
findings.recommendation: Replace `require(tx.origin == admin)` with `require(msg.sender == admin)` or use Ownable.

summary.executiveSummary: CRITICAL ALERT: Smart contract audit revealed 1 critical reentrancy vector and 1 high-risk tx.origin access control flaw. The contract MUST NOT be deployed to mainnet in its current state.
keyRisks: Complete Vault Fund Drain via Reentrant emergencyWithdraw()
Phishing Hijack of Admin Rate Controls via tx.origin
topRecommendations: Add OpenZeppelin nonReentrant modifier to emergencyWithdraw() and all state-altering functions
Change tx.origin to msg.sender across all administrative functions
Conduct comprehensive Foundry fuzz testing prior to re-submitting for audit

limitations: Analysis performed on single file repository without external oracle contracts
